title: Add and Search Words
statement:
Design a word dictionary that stores words and then finds them by a pattern, where a `.` in the pattern stands for any one letter. Write a class for the nodes your dictionary uses and a dictionary class with two operations:

- `addWord word` stores `word`.
- `search pattern` returns `true` when some stored word matches `pattern`, and `false` otherwise. A word matches when it has the same length as the pattern and the same letter at every position, where a `.` matches any letter.

The dictionary starts empty. The first line is the count `q`. Each of the next `q` lines is one operation. Words are lowercase letters only, and patterns are lowercase letters and dots. Print the answer to each `search` on its own line.

Input:

```text
7
addWord bad
addWord dad
addWord mad
search pad
search bad
search .ad
search b..
```

Expected output:

```text
false
true
true
true
```

tests.stdin:
7
addWord bad
addWord dad
addWord mad
search pad
search bad
search .ad
search b..

6
addWord apple
search app
search apple
search appl.
search apple.
search .....

6
search ...
addWord a
addWord abc
search .
search ..
search ...

7
addWord abcd
addWord abxe
addWord xbcf
search .bcf
search ab.e
search .b.d
search ..cg

9
addWord at
addWord and
addWord an
addWord add
search a
search .at
addWord bat
search .at
search an.

hints: Store the words in a trie. A pattern with no dots is an ordinary trie search, one child per letter.
At a `.` you can't pick a single child. Try every child of the current node, and the pattern matches when any of them leads to a match.
Write the search as a recursive function of a node and a position in the pattern. When the position reaches the end of the pattern, the answer is whether a word ends at that node.
